summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted for weakness and difficulty walking, following two weeks of decreased oral intake and leg swelling. She was found to be hypovolemic, likely due to continued use of high-dose diuretics while eating poorly, and was below her dry weight at admission. An enlarging cystic pancreatic mass, now measuring over 6 cm with concerning features on MRCP, raised suspicion for possible malignant transformation. Diuretics were held, IV fluids and nutritional support were initiated, and an EUS with biopsy was performed, showing low suspicion for malignancy on initial assessment, though pathology remained pending at discharge. Her platelet count dipped to 39, consistent with her known immune thrombocytopenia, and she completed a prophylactic course of ciprofloxacin post-procedure. She improved clinically, reached near dry weight, and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility with plans for close follow-up on biopsy results and heart failure management.
